detail:
NICHD states its endometriosis research aims to understand the causes and mechanisms of the condition, develop effective ways to treat pain and infertility related to it, and find ways to prevent it. A central goal the institute lists is better ways to diagnose the disease, because surgery is currently the only definitive method, and researchers are seeking less invasive ways to determine whether a person has endometriosis.

Other directions NICHD describes include better treatments for pain and infertility, noting even invasive surgical treatments do not provide definite relief for everyone, and research into causes including inflammation, epigenetics, genetics, and hormonally active environmental contaminants. The institute also highlights foundational work that supported approval of elagolix for endometriosis-associated pain and studies of new approaches in animal and human research, framed as investigational until trials confirm benefit.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about endometriosis diagnosis and treatment research.
sourceName: Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development

title: Where endometriosis research is heading
